attributes.action: Give new partners of convicted domestic abusers a statutory right to know
attributes.additional_details:
People convicted of serious domestic abuse can enter new relationships while still serving their sentence, including suspended sentences.

We want Parliament to introduce a statutory Right to Know for new partners of qualifying domestic-abuse offenders. New partners should be informed of relevant convictions and the current sentence, without needing to request a Clare's Law disclosure or prove they are at risk. This would help people make informed decisions about their safety.
attributes.background: Introduce legislation giving new intimate partners of people currently serving a sentence for serious domestic abuse a statutory right to be informed of their partner's relevant conviction and sentence.

rejection.details: For there to be a right to know there also has to be a duty on someone to provide that knowledge/information. Your petition isn't clear on who that would be - or how they would know when someone entered what you describe as an 'intimate' relationship with someone serving a domestic abuse sentence.
